original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: For the unsigned dirty connector over a ring of characteristic c (k immutable sources, all 2^k-1 nonzero binary-mask outputs, calls B_j: z += B_j x_j and A_m: y_m += A_m z), decide for which k the per-operator floor c(k+2^k-1) is attained. Answers part of PR4231 open question 1 (characteristic four) and gives a construction for every c.
scope_change_reason: Keeps the PR4231 alphabet and increases the source count, which the card lists as a scope-change trigger. PR4231 left the characteristic-four threshold open; the floor is the premise any larger-batch consumer of that alphabet would rely on.
bottleneck_link: Bounds the batch size at which a characteristic-c connector consumer can pay exactly c calls per operator. No physical consumer, admission or transfer is supplied, so no kappa change follows.
stop_rule: Stop after the block construction for k<=2c, one explicit characteristic-four walk beyond 2c, the deletion lemma and the counting exclusion. Local-search failures are reported only as search failures.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json gives a 36-event characteristic-four walk on nine sources. verify.py builds the block words for all 2<=c<=7, k<=2c, regenerates every readout of the nine-source walk, simulates literal words with generic noncommuting coefficients and dense random matrices over Z/4, checks nine deletions, an exhaustive depth-one census at k=3, counting thresholds for c<=9 and six rejection controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the exact characteristic-four threshold N(4), now known to satisfy 9 <= N(4) <= 21?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the largest batch on which the characteristic-four connector pays exactly four calls per operator.
open_questions.first_step: By the deletion lemma every ten-source floor walk restricts to a nine-source one: enumerate four-event insertions into canonical nine-source floor walks, or sharpen the counting bound by excluding boundary multisets whose sum cannot be binary.
open_questions.blocked_by: Simulated annealing over 40-event walks did not reach full coverage in the local runs; no exclusion beyond counting is proved.

open_questions.question: How does N(c) grow with c? The block construction gives N(c) >= 2c and counting gives N(c) = O(c log c).
open_questions.why_it_matters: A linear gap in the constant changes how large a batch can stay at the floor in high characteristic.
open_questions.first_step: Find blocks of depth d carrying more than 2d sources (a depth-two block on five sources at c=4 would already give ten); Lemma C shows depth one carries at most two.
open_questions.blocked_by: Local search for a depth-two five-source block at c=4 reached 28 of 31 masks; a depth-three seven-source block reached 125 of 127.

open_questions.question: Does any concrete consumer use a characteristic-c batch of more than c sources at a favorable complete invoice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The abstract call counts change no recursive supplier or kappa by themselves.
open_questions.first_step: Identify an immutable-source, unobserved-output caller with coefficients of characteristic c and price every primitive, admission and dispatch.
